the primary role of adipocytes is to store triglycerides during periods of caloric excess and to mobilize this reserve when expenditure
exceeds intake, it is now widely recognized that adipose tissue lies at the heart of a complex network participating in the regulation
of a variety of quite diverse biological functions (Fig. 1).

Development
During fetal development WAT emerges at midgestation in humans or postnatally in rodents. Although the evolutionary and devel-
opmental features of WAT and brown adipose tissue (BAT) already suggested that they are quite distinct tissues, until recently, white
and brown adipocytes were thought to be derived from the same precursor cell (Frühbeck et al., 2009b). Elegant in vivo fate mapping
experiments in mice have recently provided a clear evidence that brown adipocytes arise from a separate and distinct population of
progenitors (Fig. 2).
